abstract:
The increasing datafication of work has become a pervasive theme within organizations, particularly with the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies that rely on data and machine learning to generate insights and decisions. Prior research has shown that datafication practices aimed at administrative control and accountability can transform organizations in profound and often unintended ways. Our research moves beyond investigating datafication for administrative purposes to explore how it unfolds when actors intend to extract knowledge through AI predictive modeling. Drawing on a three-year ethnography of a human resources (HR) department introducing AI for candidate screening, we find that datafication expanded far beyond the technology’s initially envisioned scope. We explain this scope expansion by introducing the concept of
                    epistemic enchantment
                    : a collective process through which organizational members become captivated and mobilized by AI’s promise to generate predictive, objective, and continuously improving insights from data, while overlooking the costs and risks involved. Our study reveals how datafication practices can expand endlessly as organizational members, enchanted by AI’s epistemic promises, pursue the notion of ideal data as an ever-desired but never reachable goal.

ob.tldr: 基于三年HR部门民族志调查，探讨AI候选人筛选场景下数据化实践的扩张机制。研究发现，数据化远超技术最初设想范围；据此提出"认知魅惑"概念：组织成员被AI预测性、客观性、持续改进的承诺所俘获与动员，忽视成本与风险，将"理想数据"当作永恒追求却永不可及的目标。

title: In Pursuit of Ideal Data: Epistemic Enchantment and the Unintended Consequences of Datafying for Artificial Intelligence
title_zh: 追求理想数据：人工智能数据化中的认识论迷魅与意外后果
